search.dialog.title: Search

@search.dialog.title.description: Title shown at the top of the whole-drive file Search dialog. Single word naming the feature.

@search.runHint.description: Subtle hint in the right side of the search input, shown when auto-apply is off and the typed query hasn't run yet. Tells the user the search runs on Enter.

search.action.showAll.label: Show all in main window

@search.action.showAll.label.description: Primary footer button in the Search dialog. Promotes the current search results into the active file pane so the user can browse them like a folder. Activated by the keyboard shortcut shown next to it.

search.action.showAll.tooltip: Open the search results in the active pane

@search.action.showAll.tooltip.description: Hover tooltip for the 'Show all in main window' button in the Search dialog.

search.action.goToFile.label: Go to file

@search.action.goToFile.label.description: Secondary footer button in the Search dialog. Opens the file under the cursor by navigating the active pane to it. Activated by the Enter key shown next to it.

search.action.goToFile.tooltip: Open the file in the active pane

@search.action.goToFile.tooltip.description: Hover tooltip for the 'Go to file' button in the Search dialog.

@search.recent.runAria.description: Accessibility label for a recent-search chip in the Search dialog. Read aloud by screen readers; activating the chip re-runs that past search.

placeholders.mode: the search mode of the past search, already translated (for example AI, Regex, or Filename)
placeholders.query: the text the user searched for, shown verbatim and not translated

@search.recent.runAria.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.systemDirExclude.default: Excludes common system and build folders

@search.systemDirExclude.default.description: Placeholder tooltip on the 'Hide boring folders' option in the Search dialog's scope popover, shown briefly before the full folder list loads. 'build folders' are folders like node_modules that hold generated or downloaded code.

search.systemDirExclude.heading: These folders are hidden:

@search.systemDirExclude.heading.description: Heading inside the 'Hide boring folders' tooltip in the Search dialog's scope popover. Introduces the list of folder names that the search skips. The folder names themselves are not translated.

search.notAFolderToast: Search results aren''t a folder. Paste into a real folder instead.

@search.notAFolderToast.description: Toast shown when the user tries a paste, new-folder, or rename action while a pane is showing search results. Search results are a read-only view, not a real folder, so those actions can't apply there.
@search.notAFolderToast.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.searchableFolder.disabledTooltip: Current folder is search results, which isn''t searchable. Open a real folder first.

@search.searchableFolder.disabledTooltip.description: Tooltip on the disabled 'Use current folder' button in the Search dialog's scope popover. Explains that the active pane is showing search results (a read-only view), so there's no real folder to search inside.
@search.searchableFolder.disabledTooltip.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.imageResults.title: Text in images

@search.imageResults.title.description: Heading for the section of the Search dialog that shows images whose OCR-read text matches the query, rendered as a thumbnail grid below the filename results.
@search.imageResults.title.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.imageResults.count.description: Count shown next to the "Text in images" heading when every match is displayed.

placeholders.totalText: the number of matching images, already formatted for display (for example 1,240)

@search.imageResults.count.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.imageResults.countCapped.description: Count shown next to the "Text in images" heading when there are more matches than the grid displays at once.

placeholders.shownText: how many images the grid shows, already formatted (for example 48)
placeholders.totalText: the total number of matching images, already formatted (for example 1,240)

@search.imageResults.countCapped.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.imageResults.indexing: Still indexing images, so results may be incomplete.

@search.imageResults.indexing.description: Shown while a background pass is still reading text from this drive''s images, warning the user the image results aren''t complete yet.
@search.imageResults.indexing.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.imageResults.notIndexed: This drive''s images aren''t indexed yet. They''ll become searchable once indexing runs.

@search.imageResults.notIndexed.description: Shown when image indexing is on but no images on this drive have been read yet, so there''s nothing to search. Distinct from a genuine no-match.
@search.imageResults.notIndexed.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.imageResults.empty.description: Shown when this drive''s images have been indexed but none of them contain the searched text (a genuine no-match, not "not indexed yet").
@search.imageResults.empty.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.imageResults.networkOff: Turn on image indexing for this network drive in Settings to search the text inside its photos.

@search.imageResults.networkOff.description: Shown in the "Text in images" section when searching a network (SMB) drive that hasn''t been opted into image indexing. Points the user to the per-drive opt-in in Settings > Behavior > File system watching > Image search.
@search.imageResults.networkOff.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.imageResults.paused: This drive is disconnected, so these are the photos indexed so far.

@search.imageResults.paused.description: Shown when a network drive disconnected mid-indexing: what was already indexed stays searchable, and indexing resumes when the drive reconnects.
@search.imageResults.paused.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.imageResults.findSimilar.description: Label for the action (a button on each image tile) that re-runs the grid to show images that look like this one, using on-device image similarity.
@search.imageResults.findSimilar.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.imageResults.matchedDescription.description: A quiet reason line under an image tile when the image matched the search text by its VISUAL CONTENT (an on-device AI describing the photo), not by any text printed inside it. It stands in for the highlighted text snippet the keyword matches show.
@search.imageResults.matchedDescription.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.imageResults.similarTo.description: Heading shown above the grid when it's showing images similar to a chosen one, instead of text-match results.

placeholders.name: the file name of the image the results are similar to, shown verbatim (for example beach.jpg)

@search.imageResults.similarTo.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.imageResults.backToResults.description: Button that leaves the "similar images" view and returns to the text-match results for the current query.
@search.imageResults.backToResults.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.imageResults.similarEmpty.description: Shown in the "similar images" view when this drive has no images close enough to the chosen one (for example the chosen image isn't indexed yet).
@search.imageResults.similarEmpty.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.walkHandoff.running.description: Headline of the toast shown in the main window when a search kept running after the user sent its results to a pane. A spinner sits next to it. {label} is the short name of the search (the query text, or the AI-generated title).

placeholders.label: the search's short name, e.g. "*.pdf" or "tax paperwork"

@search.walkHandoff.running.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.walkHandoff.counts: {matchCount, plural, one {# match} other {# matches}} so far, {folderCount, plural, one {# folder} other {# folders}} scanned

@search.walkHandoff.counts.description: Second line of the still-searching toast: how many files matched and how many folders Cmdr has been through. No percentage or estimate, because the total is unknowable. Use matchText and folderText for the digits if your language needs them grouped.

placeholders.matchCount: number of matches so far, for plural selection
placeholders.matchText: the same number, already formatted with thousands separators
placeholders.folderCount: number of folders scanned, for plural selection
placeholders.folderText: the same number, already formatted with thousands separators

@search.walkHandoff.counts.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.walkHandoff.reopen.description: Button in the still-searching toast that brings the search dialog back, with the running search still in it. Short: it renders as a small button.
@search.walkHandoff.reopen.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.walkHandoff.stop.description: Button in the still-searching toast that stops the search. What it already found stays in the pane. Short: it renders as a small button.
@search.walkHandoff.stop.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.walkHandoff.hideTooltip: Hide this. The search keeps running.

@search.walkHandoff.hideTooltip.description: Tooltip on the still-searching toast's close (X) button, making clear that dismissing the toast doesn't stop the search (the toast has its own Stop button for that).
@search.walkHandoff.hideTooltip.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.walkHandoff.finished: {count, plural, one {Found # match} other {Found # matches}} for {label}.

@search.walkHandoff.finished.description: Toast that replaces the still-searching one when the search finishes having covered everything. It fades on its own. Use countText for the digits if your language needs them grouped.

placeholders.count: the final number of matches, for plural selection
placeholders.countText: the same number, already formatted with thousands separators
placeholders.label: the search's short name, e.g. "*.pdf" or "tax paperwork"

@search.walkHandoff.finished.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.walkHandoff.stoppedShort: The results for {label} may be short: Cmdr didn''t get through everything.

@search.walkHandoff.stoppedShort.description: Toast that replaces the still-searching one when the search ended without covering everything (stopped, the drive went away, or folders it had to give up on). It fades on its own. Reopening the search shows the detail. Avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.

placeholders.label: the search's short name, e.g. "*.pdf" or "tax paperwork"

@search.walkHandoff.stoppedShort.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.walkHandoff.superseded: Cmdr stopped adding to the results for {label}, because your new search took over.

@search.walkHandoff.superseded.description: Toast shown when the user starts a new search while an older one was still filling a pane. The pane keeps what it has; only the additions stop. It fades on its own.

placeholders.label: the older search's short name, e.g. "*.pdf" or "tax paperwork"

@search.walkHandoff.superseded.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.uncovered.local: Cmdr hasn''t indexed {drive} yet, so this search skipped:

@search.coverage.uncovered.local.description: Note above the search results when the search covered a local drive that has no index, so it had nothing to look through. A list of the skipped folder paths follows the colon, which is why the sentence ends open. Conversational; avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.

placeholders.drive: the drive's display name (e.g. Macintosh HD), or the generic phrase from search.coverage.unnamedDrive when the drive isn't mounted any more

@search.coverage.uncovered.local.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.uncovered.network: Cmdr doesn''t index network drives unless you ask, so this search skipped:

@search.coverage.uncovered.network.description: The network-drive version of search.coverage.uncovered.local, shown when the search covered a network share with no index. It explains that this is by design rather than nudging the user to index, because indexing a network drive is deliberately opt-in. A list of the skipped folder paths follows the colon.

placeholders.drive: unused here, but available so both variants take the same parameters

@search.coverage.uncovered.network.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.unresolved: {count, plural, one {Cmdr''s index doesn''t cover this folder yet, so this search skipped it:} other {Cmdr''s index doesn''t cover these folders yet, so this search skipped them:}}

@search.coverage.unresolved.description: Note above the search results when the drive IS indexed but the folder searched in isn't in that index yet (a partly indexed drive, or a path that no longer exists). It deliberately says what Cmdr knows rather than claiming the folder doesn't exist, because both cases look the same from the index. A list of the skipped folder paths follows the colon.

placeholders.count: how many folder paths were skipped, driving the singular/plural choice

@search.coverage.unresolved.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.walk.cancelled: You stopped this search, so it shows what Cmdr had found by then. Everything it read on the way is saved, so searching again picks up from there.

@search.coverage.walk.cancelled.description: Note above the search results after the user stopped a search that was reading folders the app hasn't indexed. Reassures them that stopping cost nothing: the results are real and the work already done is kept. 'Cmdr' is the product name and stays as-is. Avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.
@search.coverage.walk.cancelled.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.walk.interrupted: This search stopped early, so there may be more on {drive}. Searching again picks up where it left off.

@search.coverage.walk.interrupted.description: Note above the search results when a search that was reading folders the app hasn't indexed stopped on its own: the drive was unplugged or disconnected partway through, or a folder couldn't be opened. Not the user's doing, and not presented as a failure. Avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.

placeholders.drive: the drive's display name (e.g. Backups), or the generic phrase from search.coverage.unnamedDrive when the drive isn't mounted any more

@search.coverage.walk.interrupted.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.walk.abandoned: Some folders stopped answering, so Cmdr moved on without them and this list may be short. Searching again gives them another try.

@search.coverage.walk.abandoned.description: Note above the search results, shown when the live walk finished but gave up on one or more folders on the way (a folder that stopped responding, or a subtree it pruned after too many failed reads). It exists so a short list isn't read as an exhaustive one. Cmdr doesn't know which folders, so none are listed. Avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.
@search.coverage.walk.abandoned.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.denied: {count, plural, one {Cmdr wasn''t allowed to look inside this folder, so nothing from it is in the results:} other {Cmdr wasn''t allowed to look inside these folders, so nothing from them is in the results:}}

@search.coverage.denied.description: Note above the search results listing folders the app was refused access to, so their contents are missing from the results. A list of the folder paths follows the colon. On macOS this is usually the Full Disk Access permission, and when the app doesn't have it the offer below (search.coverage.deniedFullDiskAccess) follows. Avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.

placeholders.count: how many folders were refused, driving the singular/plural choice

@search.coverage.denied.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.deniedFullDiskAccess: With full disk access, Cmdr can search folders like these.

@search.coverage.deniedFullDiskAccess.description: Line under the list of refused folders, shown only on macOS and only when Cmdr doesn't have Full Disk Access yet. It says what would open them, and the button below it (search.coverage.setUpFullDiskAccess) goes to the setup. 'Full disk access' is the macOS permission; use the system's own wording for it in your language.
@search.coverage.deniedFullDiskAccess.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.coverage.setUpFullDiskAccess.description: Button under the refused folders that opens Cmdr's Full Disk Access setup (the same page the first-run setup shows). Short: it renders as a small button. 'Full disk access' is the macOS permission; use the system's own wording for it in your language.
@search.coverage.setUpFullDiskAccess.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.declined: {count, plural, one {Cmdr doesn''t look inside snapshot folders, so nothing from this one is in the results:} other {Cmdr doesn''t look inside snapshot folders, so nothing from these is in the results:}}

@search.coverage.declined.description: Note above the search results listing snapshot folders on a network drive, which Cmdr never looks inside on purpose: their contents are copies of files it has already seen, and one such folder can report several times the drive's real size. A list of the folder paths follows the colon. There is nothing for the user to fix, so this one explains rather than offers. Avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.

placeholders.count: how many snapshot folders were skipped, driving the singular/plural choice

@search.coverage.declined.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.stillCovering: {count, plural, one {Another search is going through this folder right now, so its files will turn up in a moment:} other {Another search is going through these folders right now, so their files will turn up in a moment:}}

@search.coverage.stillCovering.description: Note above the search results when a second search is already reading the same folders, so this one left them to it. The files aren't lost: the other search saves what it reads, so a repeat search a moment later includes them. A list of the folder paths follows the colon.

placeholders.count: how many folders another search is already reading, driving the singular/plural choice

@search.coverage.stillCovering.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.coverage.unnamedDrive.description: Stands in for a drive's name in the coverage note when the drive isn't in the live volume list any more (ejected, or a network share that disconnected). Reads inside a sentence: 'Cmdr hasn't indexed this drive yet'.
@search.coverage.unnamedDrive.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.coverage.indexDrive.description: Button in the coverage note that turns on indexing for the drive the search couldn't cover, so future searches there are instant. Short: it renders as a small button.
@search.coverage.indexDrive.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.coverage.dontAskAgain.description: Button in the coverage note that stops offering to index this drive. The note itself keeps appearing (the gap is still true); only the offer goes away. Same per-drive choice the first-connect prompt writes. Short: it renders as a small button.
@search.coverage.dontAskAgain.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.toast.started: Indexing {drive} now. Searches here will be instant once it finishes.

@search.coverage.toast.started.description: Toast confirming that indexing started after the user pressed the coverage note's Index this drive button.
@search.coverage.toast.started.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.toast.indexingOff: Drive indexing is off in Settings, so nothing indexes. Turn it on under Indexing > Drive indexing.

@search.coverage.toast.indexingOff.description: Toast shown when the coverage note's Index this drive button can't act because the master drive-indexing switch is off. Points at the settings page that owns the switch. Sentence case; avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.
@search.coverage.toast.indexingOff.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.toast.deferredUntilSearc: Cmdr is already searching {drive}. Indexing starts as soon as that finishes.

@search.coverage.toast.deferredUntilSear.description: Toast shown when the coverage note''s Index this drive button can''t start the scan yet because a search is walking the same drive. Cmdr remembers the request and runs it when the search finishes, so this is a promise, not a refusal. Avoid the words ''error'' and ''failed''.
@search.coverage.toast.deferredUntilSear.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.coverage.toast.notStarted: Cmdr can''t index {drive} right now. You can try again from the drive menu.

@search.coverage.toast.notStarted.description: Toast shown when the coverage note's Index this drive button doesn't go through (the share needs reconnecting or credentials). Points at the drive menu in the breadcrumb, which offers the same action with fuller guidance. Avoid the words 'error' and 'failed'.
@search.coverage.toast.notStarted.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.snapshot.defaultLabel.description: Fallback breadcrumb and tab title for a saved search-results view when there's no query text to name it. Same word as the dialog title.
@search.snapshot.defaultLabel.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

@search.snapshot.cappedLabel.description: Breadcrumb and tab title for a saved search-results view when the result set was too large to keep entirely, so only the first N of the total M matches are shown. The base label is the original search name.

placeholders.label: the base search label (the query or AI summary), shown verbatim
placeholders.capText: how many matches are kept, already formatted for display (for example 1,000)
placeholders.totalText: the total number of matches found, already formatted for display (for example 5,432)

@search.snapshot.cappedLabel.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.

search.runTitle: Search, including folders that aren''t indexed yet

@search.runTitle.description: Tooltip and accessibility label for the run button next to the search input, in filename and regex modes. It names what pressing it does that typing alone doesn't: the app searches beyond its index, reading folders it hasn't indexed, which can take a while and so only happens when the user asks for it.

search.coverage.pressEnter: Press Enter and Cmdr will look through it now.

@search.coverage.pressEnter.description: Line at the end of the note above the search results, shown when a search that ran on its own (as the user typed) couldn't cover everything. Pressing Enter runs the fuller search that reads the folders the app hasn't indexed. 'Enter' is the keyboard key name; 'Cmdr' is the product name and stays as-is.
@search.coverage.pressEnter.screenshotNote: Search results and the messages around them (image-text matches, index coverage, and the toasts search raises). This shows the search dialog where the query is typed and the results appear.
